items.title: Vanishing of a pro-system is equivalent to the vanishing of the limit and first derived limit of it and of its countable direct sum
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an inverse system of abelian groups (A_n) and establishes the equivalence of two conditions: that (A_n) be zero as a pro-object; and that both lim A_n and R^1 lim A_n vanish and the same holds for the countable direct sum of (A_n) (source lines 23526-23535). One direction is drawn from the pro-isomorphism statement: (1) implies (2) (proof lines 23538-23539). For the converse the proof first applies Emmanouil's criterion to conclude that (A_n) is Mittag-Leffler (proof lines 23540). The substantive part is then a direct analysis of the images: defining A_{n,m} = Im(A_m -> A_n) for m >= n, so that A_n = A_{n,n} contains A_{n,n+1} contains ..., the proof records the two translations of the hypotheses — that (A_n) is zero as a pro-object exactly when for every n there is m >= n with A_{n,m} = 0, and that (A_n) is Mittag-Leffler exactly when for every n there is m_n >= n with A_{n,m} = A_{n,m+1} = ... (proof lines 23541-23546). In the Mittag-Leffler case the proof observes that lim A_n = 0 forces A_{n,m_n} = 0, because the maps A_{n+1,m_{n+1}} -> A_{n,m} are surjective in that case, which completes the argument (proof lines 23546-23549). The non-routine content is the translation of pro-zeroness into the vanishing of the images at some later stage and the surjectivity used to descend it.
